judges.15.p1.b1.text: Later on, at the time of the wheat harvest, Samson took a young goat and went to visit his wife.

judges.15.p1.b2.text: I want to go to my wife in her room,

judges.15.p1.b3.text: But her father would not let him enter.

judges.15.p1.b4.text: I was sure that you thoroughly hated her, … so I gave her to one of the men who accompanied you. Is not her younger sister more beautiful than she? Please take her instead.

judges.15.p1.b5.text: This time I will be blameless in doing harm to the Philistines.

judges.15.p2.b1.text: Then Samson went out and caught three hundred foxes. And he took torches, turned the foxes tail-to-tail, and fastened a torch between each pair of tails.

judges.15.p2.b2.text: Then he lit the torches and released the foxes into the standing grain of the Philistines,

judges.15.p2.b3.text: burning up the piles of grain and the standing grain, as well as the vineyards and olive groves.

judges.15.p3.b2.text: It was Samson, the son-in-law of the Timnite, … For his wife was given to his companion.

judges.15.p3.b3.text: So the Philistines went up and burned her and her father to death.

judges.15.p3.b4.text: Because you have done this, I will not rest until I have taken vengeance upon you.

judges.15.p3.b5.text: And he struck them ruthlessly with a great slaughter,

judges.15.p3.b6.text: and then went down and stayed in the cave at the rock of Etam.

judges.15.p4.b1.text: Then the Philistines went up, camped in Judah, and deployed themselves near the town of Lehi.

judges.15.p4.b2.text: In response, three thousand men of Judah went to the cave at the rock of Etam,

judges.15.p4.b3.text: Do you not realize that the Philistines rule over us? What have you done to us?

judges.15.p4.b4.text: I have done to them what they did to me,

judges.15.p4.b5.text: Swear to me that you will not kill me yourselves.

judges.15.p4.b6.text: So they bound him with two new ropes and led him up from the rock.

judges.15.p5.b1.text: When Samson arrived in Lehi, the Philistines came out shouting against him.

judges.15.p5.b2.text: And the Spirit of the LORD came mightily upon him. The ropes on his arms became like burnt flax,

judges.15.p5.b3.text: and the bonds broke loose from his hands.

judges.15.p5.b4.text: He found the fresh jawbone of a donkey, reached out his hand and took it,

judges.15.p5.b5.text: and struck down a thousand men.

judges.15.p6.b1.text: With the jawbone of a donkey I have piled them into heaps. With the jawbone of a donkey I have slain a thousand men.

judges.15.p6.b2.text: And when Samson had finished speaking, he cast the jawbone from his hand;

judges.15.p6.b3.text: and he named that place Ramath-lehi.

judges.15.p7.b1.text: And being very thirsty, Samson cried out to the LORD,

judges.15.p7.b2.text: You have accomplished this great deliverance through Your servant. Must I now die of thirst and fall into the hands of the uncircumcised?

judges.15.p7.b3.text: So God opened up the hollow place in Lehi, and water came out of it.

judges.15.p7.b4.text: When Samson drank, his strength returned, and he was revived. That is why he named it En-hakkore,

judges.15.p7.b5.text: And Samson judged Israel for twenty years in the days of the Philistines.
